text:
I WAS WRONG ABOUT THE CENTRAL RISK, AND THE CORRECTION INVERTS IT.

I opened this workstream warning that a convenience wrapper collapsing relation -> compile_frame
-> plan_geometry -> geometry would erase the plan/materialize distinction, and I asked
claude-review to guard against exactly that. The API reviewer checked the mechanism instead of
reasoning about it, and the danger runs the other way.

rsa(), rdm() and contrast() ALREADY branch on plan-versus-form. R/views.R:269-273:

  view <- if (source$kind == 'plan') {
    evaluate_geometry(x, query = query, component = component)
  } else {
    query_geometry(x, query, component)
  }

Given a PLAN, these verbs go query-first and return a query_only effect_view. So a wrapper that
builds a plan and recurses lands on the CHEAP, BOUNDED, HONEST side and never materializes. The
step such a wrapper hides is plan_geometry(), and plan_geometry() performs VALIDATION, not
materialization - R/geometry-plan.R:219-257 validates relation, frame, pairing, source
capabilities and compute policy 'without reading relation blocks'. Hiding a validation step hides
nothing semantically: it either succeeds, invisibly by construction, or it throws, fully visibly.

The actually dangerous wrapper is the one I did not think of: a naive wrapper that calls
geometry(). THAT silently materializes.

BINDING RULE, replacing my warning at the top of this bead:
  A convenience wrapper MUST route through plan_geometry() and the existing query-first branch.
  It MUST NOT call geometry(). It MUST NOT accept storage = 'block'. It MUST return the same
  view class it returns today.

Honour those three and introduction.Rmd:337-339 stays literally true. The vignette's own check at
:331-333 asserts direct$values == late$values to 1e-12 - so the distinction was never about the
ANSWER. It is about what the object RETAINS and what it may therefore be asked next. That is why
hiding the plan construction is safe and hiding the materialization is not.

ONE EXCLUSION, verified: geometry_spectrum() requires a complete form (R/views.R:319) and errors
on a plan with 'A geometry spectrum requires a complete effect form.' A wrapper for it WOULD have
to materialize, which is a hidden allocation decision. Do not provide one. Let it keep failing
with a message naming geometry(plan) as the fix. Same rule for as.data.frame: safe on
effect_geometry, which is already materialized; must NOT be added for effect_geometry_plan.

SECOND CORRECTION, same source. I listed 'capability gating' as Class II wholesale. The reviewer
went through all eleven arguments lacking defaults and WITHDREW FIVE OF ITS OWN SUGGESTIONS after
checking what each actually asserts. The one that matters most is over=:

  cross_partitions() hard-codes independence = 'independent' (R/pairing.R:108 -> :17), which sets
  the estimate attribute to 'cross_generalized' (R/pairing.R:83). That is a CLAIM ABOUT THE USER'S
  DATA - that run1 and run2 estimates are statistically independent. If runs share nuisance
  regressors or came from one GLM fit across all runs, the claim is false and the cross-generalized
  estimate is no longer unbiased around zero. The package explicitly forces
  independence = 'not_independent' for self-pairs (R/pairing.R:50-53), so silently asserting the
  opposite is precisely what that machinery exists to prevent.

  over= STAYS REQUIRED. A true one-liner is therefore not available and should not be built.

  MIDDLE PATH that removes the noun without removing the claim: accept a small enumerated
  vocabulary, over = 'all_run_pairs', expanding to cross_partitions(x). The user still TYPES the
  claim; they no longer need to know the word 'pairing'.

Also kept required after checking: residual_pair_statistics(at) (defaulting to voxels() would
silently yield a diagonal-only statistic - a hidden noise-model claim), source_capabilities
(asserts properties of code the package has never run), measurement_space(id) (an auto-generated
id manufactures a fake identity in a package whose stance is that name and dimension cannot
substitute for identity).

INCONSISTENCY WORTH SOMEONE'S ATTENTION, raised by the reviewer and not by me: plan_crossnobis()
already defaults metric = shrinkage_precision() (R/crossnobis.R:213). That IS a silent statistical
choice - a shrinkage estimator picked on the user's behalf. If over= must stay explicit on
capability-claim grounds, this existing default is harder to justify than several of the defaults
I was warned off adding.
